text: Dogfood finding (2026-08-20, DOGFOOD-FINDINGS.md): 92 of 100 concepts in the lambo-dev store carry no durable embedding — interleaved in time, not one outage window; all 44 record_action Resources plus most Constraints/Logics/Entities. Semantic recall and dedup are blind to them and the damage is cumulative with no backfill path. Candidate product work: embedding-coverage counter in lambo_stats, and a re-embed backfill verb. Cause unsettled: record_action-never-embeds by design, intermittent embedder unavailability degrading hybrid to keyword, or a flush gap.

The dogfood store's embedding damage is 475 of 509 concepts, far larger than the '92 of 100' figure carried in K's motivating table — that number is stale and understates the backfill by roughly 5x. Two consequences. First, semantic recall on this store is effectively not running: any lambo_recall here matches on keywords for 93% of the corpus, so recall-quality judgements made against the dogfood graph are judgements about the keyword path, not the hybrid one. Second, this raises the value of K2's re-embed verb and its embedded/total counter in lambo_stats — the counter would have made the drift visible the day it started, and the verb is now repairing 93% of the store rather than a tenth of it. Worth re-measuring coverage before any G recall-calibration work, since calibration against a 7%-embedded corpus would measure the wrong pipeline.

CORRECTION to the same-day claim that the 512-token clamp was a plausible contributor to the unembedded-concept damage — measured against the live dogfood store 2026-08-22, it is NOT the dominant cause. Coverage is 34 embedded of 509 concepts (93% unembedded), and the gap does not track length: concepts under 400 chars are 2/247 embedded, worse than the 400-1200 band at 32/232, while 1200-2400 is 0/30. Sub-400-char concepts never reach the 512-token clamp, so something else — the originally recorded cause, the embedder unreachable or refusing silently across whole sessions — accounts for the bulk. The clamp is still real and still worth its fix (it hard-fails every long input), but it is a second failure mode, not the explanation. Recency confirms the split: the ten newest concepts are 9/10 embedded (written after the clamp fix, with the embedder up), every earlier 100-row band is 2-8%.

The dogfood embedder's capacity flags are LOAD-BEARING, not tuning (found by K1's NVIDIA leg 2026-08-22, reproduced and fixed live on the Mac rig the same day, DOGFOOD-SETUP.md updated). llama-server clamps n_batch = n_ubatch = 512 by default, so ANY input over ~512 tokens fails HTTP 500 'input too large to process' — the J3-R3-1 failure class reachable by plain input length, no network fault needed. BGE-M3 carries 8192-token capacity; the defaults throw away fifteen sixteenths of it. On a pre-J3 binary such a write applied with embedding = NULL while the receipt said 'applied', so this is a plausible contributor to the 92/100 unembedded dogfood concepts. Run with --batch-size 8192 --ubatch-size 8192 -c 8192 (long flags only; this build rejects -u), and verify with a >512-token embed, NOT /health — health passes either way, which is how it hid.

J3 round-3 residual handed outside J3, for E2E/J4: a concept applied with a NULL embedding is unfindable by semantic recall, and neither the ack, the receipt, nor a warning says so — the receipt reads 'applied — derived 1 concept(s): 1 created, 0 matched existing' with warnings: []. Pre-existing hybrid-derive degradation, not touched by these commits, but J3 is what made a fast vector-less Ok load-bearing for durability (J3-R3-1). Any E2E durability measurement must therefore assert on the STORE's embedding column, not on applied counts: 'applied' does not mean 'embedded'. Reviewer note for future rounds: read back store state with sqlite3 rather than trusting lambo_stats' applied count, and burst MULTI-AGENT as well as multi-size — round 2's single-agent-only red/green is what let J3-R3-2 through.

Re-pinned the dogfood binary to lambo-e11fb06 (lambo-for-mooshik @ e11fb06, clean tree, LAMBO_GIT_SHA set, features store-sqlite,embed-candle-metal,embed-bge). This pin carries the record_action embedder-hop fix (record_action concepts previously stored embedding NULL — everything an agent DID was invisible to semantic recall) and the new re-embed --missing-only repair verb. Ran the repair with serve stopped: backfilled 42 NULL-vector concepts, coverage 534/576 -> 576/576, contract untouched (candle BAAI/bge-m3, dim 1024). Repointed launchd from lambo-4c6fc93, restarted, verified: lease http-shared-writer pid 35655, MCP stats embedded=576/576, ledger heartbeat git_sha=e11fb06.

record_action created its Resource and Entity concepts with NULL embeddings because it had no embedder hop, so everything an agent did was reachable only by keyword or graph traversal while derive-created concepts were vector-searchable, an inversion of what recall should favour. Commit bef53e6 added the hop.

text: The 184 historical dogfood pairs at or above the 0.85 merge threshold never merged (semantic_merged stayed 0) because a pair cannot merge when the older concept had no embedding at the time the newer one was written; the embedding gap disabled deduplication as well as semantic recall.

Workstream K moves BGE-M3 in-process through candle instead of a llama.cpp server: with no transport, 'embedder unreachable' stops being a runtime state, and what remains is a startup condition such as missing or corrupt weights.
The candle adapter loads BGE-M3 weights from nrynss/bge-m3-f16-safetensors on Hugging Face, an f16 cast of BAAI/bge-m3 verified tensor by tensor (391 of 391 tensors f16-equal).

candle device selection: device = auto resolves Metal on Apple silicon and CUDA elsewhere, and refuses to start when neither accelerator exists; device = cpu is the only way to serve without an accelerator.

On Metal, a lambo serve that becomes a proxy no longer loads the model (#31): its embedder takes about 4 MB instead of about 1.4 GB, and a cached weight digest lets a start with an unchanged model read its identity in under 1 ms instead of hashing 1.1 GB.

K1's first gate is cosine parity: embed the dogfood corpus through the candle spike and through the rig's llama-server and compare; a median self-agreement below 0.99 means the pooling is wrong. Subtly wrong pooling yields plausible but wrong vectors, so recall would degrade silently.

The Mac dogfood rig embeds with in-process candle BGE-M3 on Metal (kind = candle, device = metal, 1024 dimensions). It replaced the llama-server bge_m3 embedder on 127.0.0.1:8080 in the K2 migration on 2026-08-23.
sources: paper evaluation suite lambo-2026-09-07 embedder-superseded rubric

text: Embedder canary (#176): a writer attach embeds 20 fixed phrases and compares them with the vectors pinned for that contract in store_meta; any phrase below cosine 0.99 is a drift, which catches a model change behind the same kind, model and dim.

[embedder] canary modes: verify refuses the writer attach on a drift unless --allow-embedding-mismatch is passed, warn (the default) logs it, and off skips the check. An unreachable embedder leaves the check unverified rather than refused.
Under canary = warn, a canary check that passed within the last 10 minutes is trusted without embedding again; verify embeds at every writer attach.

[embedder] related_pairs (#87, #176): given a JSON file of at least 100 labelled related-but-distinct pairs, semantic_match_threshold becomes their p99 cosine under the configured embedder, provided that sits above the canary's random-pair floor; the result is cached against the file's SHA-256.

Under lambo's framing, unrelated pairs sit near 0.5 to 0.62 cosine on BGE-M3, so a merge threshold at the random-pair level would merge every related-but-distinct pair; the canary's random-pair quantiles are a relevance floor, never a merge threshold.

G1 measured BGE-M3 on the llama.cpp rig: true recall (bare query to stored concept vector) 0.4599 to 0.6577; paraphrase merge pairs 0.6889 to 0.8984; related-but-distinct pairs 0.6348 to 0.8913; unrelated pairs 0.4999 to 0.6249.

G2 kept semantic_match_threshold at 0.85 as a calibrated decision: 0.85 already accepts the related-but-distinct pair reset password / forgot password (0.8913), and lowering it to 0.84 would accept three more related-distinct pairs while rescuing only one paraphrase.

G2 set RECENT_SCORE to 0.35, below the lowest durable true-recall hit (0.3991), so max-merge keeps the correct vector ranking; the old 0.50 recent floor masked the 'changes that do not break existing clients' query.

Under the 0.85 threshold, G records real paraphrases below it that create duplicates by design: register user / create account (0.8230), make an account / register user (0.8152), roll out the service / deploy service (0.8294).

The Mac dogfood writer is a single launchd-supervised lambo serve over HTTP on port 7700, running as agent http-shared-writer; every client connects to http://127.0.0.1:7700/mcp instead of spawning its own serve.

Provisioned the sqlite store with the new binary, repointed the launchd unit dev.lambo.dogfood from lambo-21e4cf8, restarted, and verified: lease holder http-shared-writer, ledger heartbeat git_sha=4c6fc93, graph intact (702 nodes / 554 concepts). Config unchanged: sqlite + candle BGE-M3 on Metal. Added the operator start/stop script ~/Documents/work/scripts/lambo-dogfood.sh (start|stop|restart|status|log) and verified a full stop/start cycle releases and reacquires the lease.

The launchd ThrottleInterval for dev.lambo.dogfood is 60 seconds because the default 10 s restart falls inside the 45 s single-writer lease TTL: a restarted serve would find the lease still held and exit. At 60 s every retry lands after the lease has lapsed.

Claude Code enforcement layer 2026-09-01: instructions alone do not make Claude Code follow the lambo-dogfood protocol (operator observation: other harnesses comply from AGENTS.md text; Claude Code is notorious for skipping it). Fix is mechanical, at user scope so it covers every project: ~/.claude/settings.json hooks driving ~/lambo-dogfood/hooks/lambo-hook.sh. SessionStart injects the protocol + writer health; PreToolUse denies Edit/Write/NotebookEdit until the session has made one lambo_recall (bounded at 2 denials so restricted-toolset agents cannot deadlock); PostToolUse markers track recall/derive/edit per session_id under ~/lambo-dogfood/hooks/state; Stop blocks ending a turn that edited files without a derive or record_action, once per session, honoring stop_hook_active. Every gate fails open when the writer is down. Verified live: a Write was denied, lambo_recall lifted the gate, the retry succeeded.

Dogfood ledger (the I3 snapshot): recall-first compliance was 0.0% for claude-orchestrator (0 of 22 work sequences began with lambo_recall, and 37 derives had no prior recall), against 35.2% across all agents.

The single-writer lease has a 45 s TTL (LEASE_TTL), refreshed every 15 s (LEASE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL), so a holder gets three refresh chances inside one TTL and is meant to lose the lease if it misses all three.

J1 gates everything multi-client: the serve applies its own --agent to every connected client, and lambo_reserve hard-refuses any caller whose agent_id differs — correct fail-closed behaviour that leaves every client but one without lambo's only mutual-exclusion primitive. Per-call agent_id must be accepted at the Memory level and recorded on the interaction before a proxy or shared writer can be honest.

J1 round-2 lesson: matching an error VARIANT is not matching a PATH. conflict_err matched LamboError::Conflict to surface §11 reserve conflicts, but lease_lost_error() is also a Conflict and interpolates OPERATOR_OVERRIDE (a SQL DELETE), so the fix disclosed to the model what the parent had flattened. When selectively unhiding an error class, discriminate structurally (distinct variant or typed payload, or match at the site where sources are distinguishable), never by variant alone — and probe every producer of that variant before shipping.

J2 round-3 residual coupling, handed to J3 as ONE item: the pump's un-raced client-facing writes and the uncapped `inflight` list are the same problem. answer_lost (src/mcp/proxy.rs:1457) writes one frame per in-flight id, so the ceiling J3 chooses for outstanding receipts is also the worst-case LENGTH of an un-raced write burst to a client that may not be reading. Neither §J2 nor DIAL_BUDGET's residual section says the other exists, and both undercount the writes as 'two' when there are six un-raced Self::send sites (proxy.rs:1298, 1321, 1349, 1375, 1393, 1457).

J3 resolution of the COUPLED ceiling residual handed over by J2-R2-7 / J2-R3-3. The coupling is real and its mechanism is receipt WAITING: a lambo_receipt call that waits is a long-lived in-flight request at the proxy, so N concurrent receipt waits are N entries in the pump's `inflight` list and therefore N frames in answer_lost's un-raced write burst. J3 therefore bounds BOTH ends: RECEIPT_WAIT_MAX caps how long any one wait can occupy an inflight slot, and a concurrent-waiter cap keeps the population under proxy.rs's INFLIGHT_DEPTH_WARN = 64. The queue bound itself does NOT feed the inflight list — a non-waiting ack returns immediately — so the residual's phrasing (the receipt ceiling IS the burst length) is true only of the waiting surface, and that correction belongs in the record.

Register-discipline technique that paid off twice in J2 round 2: when a stale claim is corrected, also check the claims of every constant the corrected sentence now cites. Rewriting ELECTION_BUDGET's docstring to name ELECTION_SLACK exposed a SECOND false stated reason the reviewer had not found — ELECTION_SLACK 'absorbs store-clock skew and one missed refresh interval', where a missed refresh interval is LEASE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL = 15s, three times the 5s constant, and needs no absorbing anyway (a holder gets three chances inside one TTL and is supposed to lose the lease if it misses all three). Citing a constant is a commitment to its docstring being true.

The proxy's DIAL_BUDGET is 6 seconds and bounds the client's wait: past it the dial to the holder is abandoned and the call is answered 'nothing happened, retry later'. It sits above the dial's own connect and replay budgets (about 4.1 s) and below sqlite's 8 s busy_timeout.

J3 latency claim VERIFIED at the release binary over real stdio MCP (2026-08-20, SQLite store, 20 calls, median): against the rig's live llama.cpp BGE-M3 q8_0 on CPU, a lambo_derive ack went from 14.111 ms (base 166a3c8, synchronous) to 0.048 ms (J3). That 0.048 ms is at or BELOW the same binary's ack against FixtureEmbedder (0.076 ms), which is what 'the embedder is no longer in the call' means. Both runs applied all 21 concepts, so the fast number is not a fast no-op. The absolute figures differ from the doc's 27 ms warm derive because that was the dogfood client stack on pinned 3039b82; the delta is what J3 owns.

J3 redesign round-1 review VERDICT: REQUEST_CHANGES. One P1 (transient embedder outage at attach burns the durable backlog), three P2 (untested timeout deviation; twelve estimator-era stated reasons incl. two production log lines; the reversed pin's undeclared blast radius), one P2-candidate unconfirmed (un-migrated store voids the invariant), six P3. The founding invariant HOLDS at the binary: 64 acked == 1 applied-with-embedding + 63 durable intents at a clean close, replay applies all 63, final store 64 embedded / 0 NULL / 0 unconsumed, reproduced at an independently built binary; and at kill -9 nothing is durable and nothing claims to be. What does not hold is the durable half's promise of EVENTUAL APPLICATION. Review written to dev-diary/adversarial-review/adve-review-mooshik-J3-redesign-round1.md but NOT COMMITTED — the same macOS TCC revocation that interrupted the first run persists: bash cannot reach the repo at all (git, cargo, rg all denied), and even the Read tool is restricted to a per-file allowlist, so gates could not be re-run in this pass, the live matrix could not be extended, and no commit could be made.

Closed J3 durable-intent redesign review round 1: REQUEST_CHANGES, 1 P1 / 3 P2 / 1 unconfirmed P2 / 6 P3. Review file written but UNCOMMITTED — macOS TCC revoked filesystem access mid-session, so bash/git/cargo return Operation not permitted for the orchestrator and every subagent; no further lambo work possible until the operator grants Full Disk Access. P1 (N1): a transient embedder outage at attach destroys the whole durable-intent backlog — replay runs unconditionally with no liveness check, the failure arm cannot distinguish a content refusal from an unreachable embedder (a distinction THIS branch created by making the timeout an Err), and replay-failure consumes; J2's lease TTL aims the attach at the outage. The redesign's own deviation voids the WAL's acked-implies-eventually-applied promise. Invariant itself verified at an independently built binary including kill -9 (receipts do not lie; 64 lost with the tail as declared; undeclared consequence: post-crash replay blocked for the remaining lease TTL with restart_lost receipts in that window). Deviations: timeout arm upheld on argument, rejected as stated and untested (boundary in code is the STORE capability not the embedder, so default config fails every write on a dead llama, undeclared); Part-2 deferral upheld; intent_durable upheld as necessary. Twelve estimator-era stated reasons survive in writeq.rs including two production log lines claiming measured bounds. PAUSED by operator instruction before remediation.

J3 acks a derive once its intent is durable in the write queue, before the embedder runs; the receipt (lambo_receipt) later reports applied, refused or lost, and is the only place a write's real outcome appears.
Lambo agent roles: all remediation runs on Opus, and whole-workstream end-to-end review runs on Fable; per-task review also runs on Opus.

Post-J plan (operator, 2026-08-20): after J closes (J3 → J4 → J5 → phase close with rig re-pin + DOGFOOD-SETUP rewrite in one commit), run an END-TO-END adversarial review + remediation cycle over the whole branch — precedent: the adve-review-e2e-* and full-stack-sweep reviews — covering everything J landed as one system (identity + proxy + async acks + ledger states) rather than per-task. Then start workstream D (event-time clock, D1→D2), expected to run hours; D is the only remaining blocker of other work (C2) and carries the phase's built-in day-2 fallback decision point. Order after D: C (SoloPolicy; C1 may ride alongside D), the embedding-backfill/re-embed verb before A, H1 before B0, then B (pgvector service container, no cockroach), A parallel to B if attention allows, E last. H2 parked (no DSN); H3 runs sqlite/postgres/memory parity.

Workstream I (observability) runs before all further implementation cycles — decided 2026-08-19. Lambo is strong on state observability (canonization audit rows, stats, the store, serve-web) but has no flow record: recall scores vanish with the response and a fired blast-radius warning exists only in the conversation that saw it, which is unverifiable and therefore unclaimable. Every cycle run before I lands is dogfood data lost.

Workstream B is extract-then-extend, not copy-then-edit: B0 extracts PgStore<D: Dialect> from the hardened Cockroach adapter (move-only commit first, then carve), with postgres and cockroach as dialect files. A function enters the shared base only when its SQL is byte-identical across dialects — never forced together with a bool parameter. Copy-then-edit was rejected: it makes Postgres a second-class citizen and dual maintenance reliably fails (F-R2-2 demonstrated it).

Alias split: config strings postgres/pg resolve to PgStore<PostgresDialect>, cockroach/crdb to PgStore<CockroachDialect> — nothing maps across the boundary. This is a recorded behaviour change that fails loud, never silently mis-ranks: the Postgres dialect's CREATE EXTENSION vector and <=> operator do not exist on Cockroach, so cross-misconfiguration dies at provision or first vector query.

J1 round-3 advisory (J1-R3-3, caps.rs not J1): the INVISIBLE_RANGES decision recorded at is_disallowed_format states U+2028/U+2029 meet the table's own 'invisible structural character' criterion, then declines on the ground 'content already permits 
, so a forced line break buys an author nothing' — which answers the break half but not the invisibility half that is the criterion. Its revisit trigger ('if content ever stops permitting 
') is therefore the wrong trigger; the condition that makes the gap matter is a renderer treating U+2028 differently from 
, and serve_web plus any terminal already do. The conclusion is nevertheless right, and for a stronger reason the docstring does not give: normalize_tokens splits on char::is_whitespace(), which includes U+2028/U+2029, so a U+2028 in content cannot fork a canonical key (verified — the two contents merged). Separately, INVISIBLE_RANGES also jumps the unassigned Default_Ignorable codepoints U+2065, U+FFF0..U+FFF8, U+E0080..U+E00FF and U+E01F0..U+E0FFF: all four probed pass check_size while rendering as nothing, which is the table's stated criterion.
0.7.0 (#171): keyword recall p50 went from 18.7 ms to 7.5 ms, and 16 concurrent clients from 63 to 1,104 recalls per second, measured end to end over MCP on a 9,500-concept SQLite store.

0.7.0 (#171): a back-to-back lambo_derive is acknowledged in 0.8 ms p50 instead of 24.8 ms and applied in 6.3 ms instead of 32.4 ms, because a wake-triggered daemon cycle within 25 ms of the previous one waits out the gap and the burst shares one rescore.

0.7.0 (#171): lambo provision records a clean #148 re-key pass in store_meta (canonical_key_rule) and later provisions skip the scan; a pass that leaves a collision records nothing, and --rekey forces the full pass. On a 9,508-concept store provision takes 5.6 ms instead of 143 ms.

SQLite vectors are packed f32 since 0.7.0 (#55): on a 3,600-concept store at dim 1024 the file shrank from 47.3 MB as text to 17.1 MB, and decoding every vector from 161 ms to 3.4 ms; round-trips are bit-exact.

Structural recall is fast again in 0.7.0 (#165): anchor resolution Unicode-normalized every concept per query, about 260 ms on a 9,100-concept store; ASCII text now skips normalization, so a query takes about 1 ms instead of about 70 ms in a release build.
0.7.0 (#171): the cosine kernel accumulates in 16 independent lanes in a fixed order, so the compiler vectorizes it and every target scores the same bits; the vector scan sorts only the top k.

0.5.0 (#116): with 8 agents, 0.4.0 failed 249 of 519 writes ('hybrid derive could not commit after 8 concurrent graph changes'); 0.5.0 applied 522 of 522, and with 16 agents 1,999 of 1,999, none failed or dropped.

0.5.0 (#102): a derive's commit write-lock hold fell from 6.8 ms to 16.5 µs at 10,000 concepts, from 36.2 ms to 17 µs at 50,000, and from 168 ms to 21 µs at 100,000; every recall and write on the session used to wait behind it.
0.5.0 (#116 review): a parent_of pair or a record_action edge that would close a cycle in an acyclic relationship is refused with nothing written, and the caller is told why.

0.5.0 (#117): a write the close could not flush answers the receipt state close_unflushed instead of 'durable intent', and a lease refusal reports the lease row's facts (last refresh, expiry) instead of claiming the holder is alive.

0.4.0 (#22) added the embeddinggemma2 embedder (feature embed-eg2), which runs EmbeddingGemma 2 on llama-server and embeds text, and images when the server is started with --mmproj, into one space. Every image is sent as a lossless PNG whose longer side is 768 px.
0.4.0 (#101): stdio and the session endpoint refuse a request over 4 MiB before parsing it, as HTTP already did.
0.4.0 (#23): lambo erase-session erases a whole session in one transaction on every store and leaves a tombstone that no writer can take over.

0.4.0 (#4, #92): lambo serve-web serves an allowlist of sessions; each [[web.credential]] token has its own read scope, and without a credential the portal checks Host against DNS rebinding and sends a strict Content-Security-Policy.
0.4.0 (#18): [recall] kind = "elastic" (feature recall-elastic) mirrors each flush to an Elasticsearch index that serves recall's vector leg; the store stays the source of truth.
0.5.0 (#111): embed-candle-cuda builds against CUDA 13.4 directly and no longer needs CUDARC_CUDA_VERSION=13030.

0.6.0 (#33): a serve can hold one session per project and layer a shared session such as general under each ([serve] layers, per-project URLs /mcp/s/<session>); recall merges the layers and says which session each hit came from.
A shared-layer hit must be similar to the query by vector; a keyword match alone no longer admits it (#157, floor 0.50).
0.6.0 (#129): with repo_scope, README.md in two repositories is two concepts, not one hub; recall and inspect show the repository, and an ambiguous lookup is refused rather than guessed.

Unreleased (#179): any concept that a newer concept contradicts, more recently than anything that supports it, carries the Contradicted warning. Before, against only flagged a Canonical or Venerable concept.

Unreleased (#179): an ordinary contradicted hit must earn its own place in the first top_k; when it does, its contradicting concept is added beside it, past top_k if needed, at most one extra hit per contradicted hit, carrying companion_of.

Unreleased (#197): GC no longer collects the correction of a contradicted ordinary concept; a sweep protects the correction of every contradiction the detector reports, as long as the contradicted concept is still in memory. Concepts that only contradict each other keep none of themselves alive.

0.6.0 (#19): against on lambo_derive and lambo_record_action records that a write shows an existing concept to be wrong. A contradiction never changes a score or a status and no longer counts as a GC connection.

Unreleased (#196): contradictions get a hot-list budget, hot_list_contradiction_max (default half of hot_list_max); over it the lowest-priority contradictions are dropped first, and a full budget keeps the most recently declared ones.
0.6.0 (#20): with canonization_supersede = true (off by default), a contradicting concept that earns its own newer evidence demotes the Canonical concept it contradicts, and the audit records why.

Unreleased (#193): hybrid derive no longer merges a new concept by vector similarity into a concept whose text names different identifiers (digit runs or identifier tokens such as v0.5.0, src/mcp/server.rs, round3), so 'release v0.5.0 is current' and 'release v0.6.0 is current' stay two facts at any cosine.

0.7.0 (#178): lambo canon alias-preview --similar suggests alias pairs from 3-gram MinHash and vector cosine, with identifier, digit, type and contradiction guards and an accept/reject overrides file; it only suggests, nothing is merged.

0.7.0 (#148): canonical keys no longer stem identifier tokens, so distinct identifiers no longer merge through the key. Run lambo provision once with no session holder: it re-keys older concepts in one transaction, refuses while any session lease is live, and a rerun changes nothing; concepts the old rule had already merged stay merged.

0.6.0 (#36): canonization promotes rulings, not artifacts: support comes from the concepts that depend on a ruling, counted by their distinct origin interactions with the ruling's own origin excluded, so several dependents from one interaction count once.
Agents cite rulings by id in depends_on; lambo canon dry-run and alias-preview show the effect on a backup before it happens.

Across the five J0 agent runs, before the protocol block existed in prompts, zero lambo calls were made, although AGENTS.md obliged it and every agent had read AGENTS.md: compliance came from the prompt, not the agent's judgement or the tool's affordances.
dedup_rate.py over the early ledger window: 7 write calls, 24 concepts created, 2 matched, a dedup rate of 0.077; j1-reviewer-r1 was the only agent to match anything (0.333).

The recall-twice protocol: recall the topic before reading code, then a targeted recall on the real names afterwards. It came from the J0 arithmetic-deviation reasoning (accepted − written − write_failed), which was in the graph all along but only findable once the reader knew the key name.

Before the J1 re-pin, every write from every subagent was attributed to claude-orchestrator, so from the graph's side there had only ever been one agent and independent multi-agent convergence was impossible; the swarm-policy clock had not started.

The 2026-08-27 fair test is precision and recall against ground truth named before the fact: do the four canon-shaped invariants promote while the other ~96 concepts do not. Either direction failing is a finding.

Ground truth for the fair test, the four canon-shaped invariants: (1) the lease stays, a proxy moves the call not the write; (2) the wedge invariant, never acquire a lease you cannot serve; (3) the cooperative-identity ruling; (4) the async-ack rule, a write may be acked asynchronously only when its result does not gate the caller's next action.

Blast radius cannot fire on concepts nobody linked: the orchestrator's derives are mostly free-floating prose with almost no parent_of pairs, so 'nothing is load-bearing' is partly a statement about how agents write; nothing on the write surface nudges a caller to declare what a constraint supports.

Two-product probe (2026-08-20, J2-L1): cursor-agent scrubs TMPDIR from its MCP child while opencode passes macOS's per-user TMPDIR through, so the same binary, store and session derived two endpoint directories and cross-client memory was silently absent on default wiring.

Server-side wait budgets must fit under client spawn gates (J2-L2): serve's 50 s lease-lapse wait exceeded opencode's ~32 s MCP startup tolerance, turning a recoverable wait into 'server unavailable, no tools'.

J2-R1-1 reproduced against real products: with the holder killed mid-call, the proxy saw the closed connection in 18 ms but sent the client nothing, and the client hung 121.7 s, exactly its configured timeout (MCP error -32001).
cursor-agent needs --trust and --force for lambo's MCP tools, otherwise every MCP tool call is silently rejected; macOS also has no timeout(1).

G3 spike (2026-08-21): the dogfood graph had 386 concepts in 41 components; the giant component held 92% of Resources and 85% of Entities but only 37% of Logic and 30% of Observation concepts, because lambo_derive writes only intra-call CoOccurrence cliques plus the rarely used parent_of, while record_action links artifacts to shared file and commit hubs.
Recall phase-2 expansion follows out-edges only: 248 of 386 single seeds expand to nothing, and symmetrizing the same BFS multiplies expansion 2 to 4 times for one function call.

G3: the exclusivity filter hides pillars. A dependent with path multiplicity is excluded by construction, so 156 of 159 counted pairs sit at identical resistance; the J3-implementation concept had 13 dependents yet blast_radius 4, below the warning bar, while a pendant-6 concept warns.
